bastion_user.description: SSH user on the bastion (defaults to `user`).

host.description: SSH hostname or IP address of the target machine.

private_key.description: PEM-encoded private key contents. Conflicts with `private_key_path`.

private_key_path.description: Path to a PEM private key file. Conflicts with `private_key`.

ssh_agent.description: Use the local SSH agent (`SSH_AUTH_SOCK`). Defaults to true when no key is set.

systemd_version.description: Pin the target systemd release (e.g. `251`) for directive availability checks instead of detecting it on the host.

user.description: SSH user (default `root`).

verify.description: Validate unit files with the target host's own systemd parser (`systemd-analyze verify`), so the rules match the remote systemd version. `off` skips validation, `warn` (default) reports diagnostics without failing the apply, `error` fails the apply and rolls the file back.

block.description: Manage systemd units and networkd files on remote hosts over SSH (SFTP + systemctl/networkctl).

active.description: Whether the unit should be started (`systemctl start` / `stop`). Start failure fails the apply.

content.description: Raw file contents. Mutually exclusive with `section` blocks. When using `section`, this is computed from the rendered INI.

enable.description: Whether the unit should be enabled (`systemctl enable` / `disable`).

id.description: Resource identifier used in Terraform state.

name.description: Unit filename ending with `.automount`. Forces replacement when changed.

Manages a systemd `.automount` unit under `/etc/systemd/system`. Usually paired with a `.mount` unit.

data.description: Credential content. Never read back from the remote host, but persisted in Terraform state (marked `Sensitive`) — treat state as secret.

encrypted.description: Encrypt the credential with `systemd-creds encrypt` under `/etc/credstore.encrypted` (default `true`) instead of storing it as plaintext under `/etc/credstore`. Forces replacement when changed, since flipping this switches the remote path (`/etc/credstore` vs `/etc/credstore.encrypted`) and an in-place update would orphan the credential at the old path.

id.description: Resource identifier used in Terraform state.

name.description: Credential filename under the credstore (e.g. `db-pass`). Forces replacement when changed.

with_key.description: Key source passed to `systemd-creds encrypt --with-key` (`auto`, `host`, `tpm2`, or `host+tpm2`). Only meaningful when `encrypted = true`.

block.description: Manages a systemd credential in the host credential store, consumable by units via `LoadCredential=` (plaintext, `/etc/credstore/{name}`) or `LoadCredentialEncrypted=` (encrypted with `systemd-creds`, `/etc/credstore.encrypted/{name}`). `data` is never decrypted or read back from the remote host, so Terraform trusts state/config for drift — but that also means the secret **is stored in Terraform state** (as a `Sensitive` attribute). Treat state as secret.

block.description: Directives of the systemd `[Unit]` section, typed as properties with systemd validation rules. Mutually exclusive with `section` blocks for the directives declared here.
Manages a systemd `.slice` unit under `/etc/systemd/system` (cgroup resource hierarchy).

active.description: Whether the unit should be started (`systemctl start` / `stop`). Start failure fails the apply.

Manages a systemd unit file under `/etc/systemd/system/{name}` on a remote host over SSH.

id.description: Same as `name`.

name.description: Interface name (e.g. `eth0`).

setup_state.description: Parsed setup state from `networkctl status` when present.

block.description: Reads networkd link status via remote `networkctl status`.

id.description: Link name, or `global` when unset.

link.description: Optional interface name. When unset, returns global status.

block.description: Reads systemd-resolved status via remote `resolvectl status [link]`.

id.description: Same as `name`.

name.description: Unit filename (e.g. `sshd.service`).

block.description: Reads systemd unit status via remote `systemctl show`.

id.description: Same as `version`.

block.description: Reads the systemd release of the target host (`systemctl --version`). Use it to gate or branch unit configurations on the remote systemd version; unit file validation always uses this same version via `systemd-analyze verify`.
